identify_accident_scenario.failure_modes: Model defaulted to a generic explosion/release template: it overfilled optional nodes with unsupported or "Not specified" entries, treated observed manifestations (overpressure/explosion/release) as causal events, and ignored upstream mechanistic cause information available in same-incident analysis sections. It also chose released byproducts instead of the direct triggering material, and copied hazard-consequence evidence that was not a clean direct quote.
identify_accident_scenario.patch_rules: 1. Only emit nodes that are required by the SCHEMA or clearly supported and causally essential; do not add optional nodes just to say "Not specified". 2. Do not use consequence/manifestation wording (overpressure, explosion, blast, ejection) as the InitiatingEvent when the report provides an upstream mechanism; prefer the earliest causal abnormal mechanism. 3. If same-incident analysis/cause sections describe a direct precursor chain, use them to define InitiatingEvent and MechanicalFailure, and you may summarize tightly linked precursor steps into one initiating event. 4. For confined internal explosion/overpressure scenarios, do not assume a separate release/dispersion/ignition sequence; omit IgnitionSource, ReleaseType, Dispersion, IntermediateEvent, etc. unless explicitly evidenced and required. 5. Select the single material that directly triggers the hazard consequence; derive Phase/Volatility from that selected material, not from all emitted materials. 6. If IDENTIFIED_HAZARD_CONSEQUENCE evidence is paraphrased or non-verbatim, keep the node identity but replace evidence with a short direct quote from the incident text.

causal_edge_linking.failure_modes: The prompt over-restricts `has` to Material→Condition, so the model avoided valid characterization edges such as equipment/location→condition and condition→hazard classification. It also treated manifestation/restatement nodes (e.g., overpressure event, large explosion) as causal intermediates, producing redundant or reversed chains instead of linking underlying mechanisms to the resulting condition/hazard. Finally, it relied on surface chronology/wording (“overpressure event”) rather than semantic role, reversing some event↔condition directions.
causal_edge_linking.patch_rules:
1. Expand `has`: allow any direct characterization edge, not just Material→Condition; use it for Entity/Location/Equipment → inherent Condition/state, and for immediate defining Condition → HazardConsequence when the condition is part of the hazard’s classification.
2. Do not use manifestation/restatement nodes as upstream causes of the same phenomenon; if an event merely rephrases the hazard or a condition, omit redundant chains unless the text gives a distinct intermediate mechanism.
3. When an initiating mechanism produces a resulting state, orient Event → Condition (e.g., mechanism → high pressure), not Condition → Event when the event name is just that condition manifested.
4. Prefer earliest direct physical mechanism nodes over later observed manifestations; avoid duplicate event→event→hazard chains.
